newsitem.title: PERU: J.P. Morgan opens office in Peru.
newsitem.headline: J.P. Morgan opens office in Peru.

text.p: U.S. investment bank J.P. Morgan announced Thursday the opening of offices in Peru which it hailed as a country with solid growth prospects.

"It is clear that we have very optimistic perspectives for Peru because the economic measures of recent years promote fundamental reforms towards a healthy and sustained growth," J.P. Morgan vice-president Roberto Mendoza told reporters.
"We want to show our clients that there are great opportunites to invest and make money here."

The company's vice-president for Latin America, and head of the new office in Lima, Susana De La Puente, said Peru was an "interesting investment possibility" and investors had not been put off by recent internal political problems plaguing President Alberto Fujimori.

"The political events should not stop the deepening of the economic system and the dialogue with the international community," she said. "Investors see the political debate as the evolution of the country to forge a solid democracy."
Fujimori's approval ratings have slipped to their lowest level in his seven-year rule -- around 30 percent -- on the public's perception of his authoritarian style.
